--- title: "Uniform Deployment: Separating Advective from Deployment Sampling Bias" jupyter: python3 --- ```{=html} ``` The permutation test of `theory.tex` rests on **D1a** (constant design mean, $\mathbb{E}[w^{(l)}]=\bar w$ for every velocity year $l$). The companion report finds D1a decisively violated for real Argo deployment geometry. This report asks what happens when the deployment design is replaced by one that is uniform with respect to the analysis measure $\mathbb{P}$, and what the answer implies for the test. The motivation is a decomposition. Running both deployment designs through the *same* velocity years splits the total sampling bias exactly, by definition rather than by assumption: $$\underbrace{\big\langle w[\omega_{\mathrm{argo}}, V_k] - p,\ \tilde Z_k \big\rangle}_{B_{\mathrm{tot}}} \;=\; \underbrace{\big\langle w[\omega_{\mathrm{unif}}, V_k] - p,\ \tilde Z_k \big\rangle}_{B_{\mathrm{adv}}\ \text{(advective)}} \;+\; \underbrace{\big\langle w[\omega_{\mathrm{argo}}, V_k] - w[\omega_{\mathrm{unif}}, V_k],\ \tilde Z_k \big\rangle}_{B_{\mathrm{dep}}\ \text{(deployment design)}}$$ $B_{\mathrm{dep}}$ is the excess attributable to real deployment design *given the flow*; it contains the deployment $\times$ advection interaction and is not "what deployment would do without advection". This report characterises the first term. # Why the first control arm was invalid An earlier uniform arm reported $\mathrm{SS}_A = 0.93$ with $p = 1.0000$ at 4999 permutations — *every* replicate exceeded the observed statistic. That is not agreement with the null; under a true null the $p$-value is uniform, so $p = 1.0000$ is itself a $1/5000$ event. It was the symptom of four defects, all now fixed: | defect | consequence | |---|---| | RNG keyed on replicate, not `(year, rep)` — the same seeds reused in every year | designs paired across years, violating Lemma 1's $\omega_{l,d}\overset{iid}{\sim}\mathcal{D}$. Between-year variation carried no seed noise while the permutation null did, biasing the test to non-rejection | | latitude uniform in **degrees** | $1/\cos(\mathrm{lat})$ tilt, 16% across box B: $w \neq p$ at $t=0$, putting a deployment component into the advective arm | | all floats released 1 Jan | one cohort ageing together, not a standing stock | | margin $4^\circ$ (445 km lat, 341 km lon) $<$ the 730 km rms annual displacement | box starved of inflow from the band that should supply it | | lifespans set to zero, disabling the mortality kernel | uniform floats never died while argo floats retired — the arm contrast confounded geography with mortality | Re-analysed with a **blocked** permutation (year labels permuted within replicate, which respects the pairing), that same data gives $p = 0.344$ rather than $1.0000$ — an ordinary value, and the correct way to read the old arm. # The corrected specification `code/osse/design_invariance.py`, `--source uniform`: - **equal-area latitude**, $\mathrm{lat} = \arcsin\!\big(U(\sin \mathrm{la}_0, \sin \mathrm{la}_1)\big)$, so the seed measure is $\mathbb{P}$ restricted to the seeded region; - **uniform day-of-year release**, giving an age mixture rather than a single cohort; - **margin $8^\circ$**, exceeding the annual rms displacement; - **lifespans drawn from the same empirical Argo pool** as the real-deployment arm, so the two arms differ in deployment design alone; - **RNG keyed on `(year, rep)`**, satisfying Lemma 1. Release times stay inside the velocity year: the design must be a function of $(\omega, V_l)$ alone, so a float cannot be advected by a neighbouring year's flow. Within-year staggering is therefore the most age-mixing available without breaking that, and the array still ramps from empty — which is why 160 floats are deployed to hold a mean standing stock near the 50 of the real array. Verification of the sampler, at 200,000 draws: latitude flat against the equal-area expectation ($\chi^2/\mathrm{df} = 0.84$, edge ratios 0.996 and 1.004, against the 1.15 tilt degrees-uniform would give); longitude and day-of-year uniform; lifespan median matching the pool at 1339 d; and seeds differing across years. # What was simulated One array task per velocity year, 2010–2019, each drawing **190 independent seedings** of 160 floats and advecting them at the 1000 m park depth for 360 days with positions every 10 days. Replicates are only labels on one `ParticleSet`, so $R$ seedings of $n$ floats cost the same as one run of $R\times n$ — and because the seeds are iid and the flow is common, they are exactly $R$ iid draws of $\omega$ through $V_l$. That yields **1895 designs** and 1.01M in-box profiles. ::: {.callout-note collapse="true"} ## A mask-coverage artefact, and why the analysis is restricted to fully-wet cells Profiles are binned by position alone, but $p_j$ counts only water below the 2000 m analysis depth. On the Grand Banks and Flemish Cap a $1^\circ$ cell can be 2% wet, so $\mathbb{E}[w]/p$ there reaches **42**, swamping every map. 6.5% of weight lands in cells under 50% coverage. `sample_residuals.py` drops profiles whose containing native cell is masked, so those profiles never enter $B$ in the first place. All results below therefore restrict to the **167 fully-wet cells** of 220, renormalising $w$ and $p$ over that support — the support the estimator actually uses. On it, $\mathbb{E}[w]/p$ has median 1.00 and 5–95% range 0.94–1.05. ::: # Where advection concentrates a uniform deployment $\mathbb{E}[w^{(l)}]/p$ per velocity year. Values above 1 mark cells that a deployment uniform with respect to $\mathbb{P}$ over-occupies once advected; this *is* $B_{\mathrm{adv}}$'s weight vector. ::: {#cell-fig-excess .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} fig = dm.plot_excess_maps(mean, p) plt.show() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ![Advective concentration of a P-uniform deployment, per velocity year. log2 of E[w]/p on the 167 fully-wet cells; red over-occupied, blue under-occupied.](uniform_deployment_files/figure-html/fig-excess-output-1.png){#fig-excess width=1321 height=514} ::: ::: ::: {#tbl-excess .cell execution_count=3} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=27} ```{=html}
quantity E[w]/p
0 median 0.998
1 5th pct 0.866
2 95th pct 1.143
3 min 0.723
4 max 1.325
``` ::: ::: Advection moves a uniform deployment only modestly: the middle 90% of cells sit within $\pm 6\%$ of $p$, with the full range across all years and cells spanning 0.72–1.33. The structure is persistent across years rather than idiosyncratic — the same features recur in every panel, which is what makes the *between-year* question below the interesting one. # Does D1a hold under uniform deployment? The Monte Carlo makes this answerable in a way one replicate per year cannot: each year's $\mathbb{E}[w^{(l)}]$ is estimated with a standard error, so the between-year spread of those means can be judged against it. If D1a held exactly, the spread would equal the Monte-Carlo error and the ratio would be 1. ::: {#cell-fig-snr .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} fig = dm.plot_d1a_snr(tab) plt.show() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ![Between-year sd of E[w] divided by the Monte-Carlo standard error of each year's mean. A ratio of 1 (red line) is what pure sampling noise produces.](uniform_deployment_files/figure-html/fig-snr-output-1.png){#fig-snr width=1198 height=451} ::: ::: ::: {#tbl-snr .cell execution_count=5} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=29} ```{=html}
statistic value
0 median ratio 1.020
1 fraction of cells > 1 0.521
2 fraction of cells > 2 0.000
``` ::: ::: Median 1.02 with 52% of cells above 1 and none above 2 — the profile of an effect sitting essentially at the noise floor. But "at the noise floor per cell" is not "absent", and aggregating over 167 cells with 190 replicates each resolves it: ::: {#tbl-effect .cell execution_count=6} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=30} ```{=html}
variant designs cells SS_A null_median noise floors p-value
0 argo 100 167 4.7753 1.1918 4.0067 0.001
1 uniform 1895 167 1.7274 1.4343 1.2044 0.001
``` ::: ::: **D1a is rejected for both arms.** With enough replicates a small residual violation is always detectable, so significance alone is uninformative here; the effect size is what matters. On the common scale of $\mathrm{SS}_A$ divided by its own permutation-null median, the real-deployment arm sits at **4.0 noise floors** and the uniform arm at **1.2**. Subsampled to the argo arm's 10 replicates, the uniform arm gives $\mathrm{SS}_A$ of 1.59 (5–95%: 1.39–1.78) — argo's 4.89 exceeds 100% of those draws. So uniform deployment does not rescue D1a. It shrinks the violation by roughly $3.3\times$. The residual is the mechanism of uniformly-seeded floats advecting into year-varying concentration, which no deployment design can remove because it is a property of the flow. ::: {#cell-fig-pcoa .cell execution_count=7} ``` {.python .cell-code} coords = pcoa[["pcoa1", "pcoa2"]].to_numpy() yrs = pcoa["vel_year"].to_numpy() years = np.unique(yrs) cmap = plt.get_cmap("viridis", len(years)) fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6.6, 5.6)) for i, y in enumerate(years): m = yrs == y ax.scatter(coords[m, 0], coords[m, 1], s=8, alpha=0.4, color=cmap(i), label=str(y)) ax.scatter(*coords[m].mean(0), s=150, marker="*", color=cmap(i), edgecolor="k", lw=0.6, zorder=3) ax.set_xlabel(f"PCoA 1 ({100*pcoa['frac1'][0]:.1f}%)") ax.set_ylabel(f"PCoA 2 ({100*pcoa['frac2'][0]:.1f}%)") ax.legend(fontsize=7, ncol=2, markerscale=1.6) plt.show() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ![PCoA of Hellinger distances between all 1895 designs, coloured by velocity year; stars mark year centroids. Heavily overlapping clouds with barely separated centroids is the visual form of a 1.2-noise-floor effect.](uniform_deployment_files/figure-html/fig-pcoa-output-1.png){#fig-pcoa width=655 height=544} ::: ::: # Implications for the permutation test The uniform arm is not only a diagnostic — it is a design the test can actually be run on, because its D1a violation is small. Evaluating $\tilde Z_k$ at all 1.01M profile positions (`sample_residuals.py`, a strict cell-day lookup) gives $B$ for every design and analysis year, and the test follows directly. ::: {#tbl-perm .cell execution_count=8} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=32} ```{=html}
analysis year T_k (GJ/m2) permutation sd T_k / sd p_k (max-T, FWER)
0 2015 -0.0104 0.0441 -0.24 1.0000
1 2016 -0.0094 0.0554 -0.17 1.0000
2 2017 -0.0765 0.0518 -1.48 0.5282
3 2018 -0.1487 0.0510 -2.92 0.0169
4 2019 -0.1096 0.0545 -2.01 0.2040
``` ::: ::: ::: {#cell-fig-perm .cell execution_count=9} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ![Permutation null of Tbar over 10,000 relabellings of the velocity-year label, with the observed value marked.](uniform_deployment_files/figure-html/fig-perm-output-1.png){#fig-perm width=647 height=357} ::: ::: Every $T_k$ is negative, and 2018 survives family-wise correction on its own. **This is a rejection of $H_0$ under a deployment design that is uniform by construction.** The sign says floats advected by year-$k$'s flow sample year-$k$'s residual field *low* — they end up where that year's OHC anomaly is below the domain mean. ## Is it drift, or is it real? The rejection above assumes D1a, which the previous section shows is violated at 1.2 noise floors. That contamination has to be ruled out before the result can be believed, and the placebo comparison does it without assuming D1a at all: apply each year's design contrast $\Delta_k$ to *other* years' fields, which it cannot have been shaped by. Under pure drift the matched (diagonal) values are unremarkable against the off-diagonal spread. ::: {#tbl-placebo .cell execution_count=10} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=34} ```{=html}

2016 0.0134 -0.0094 -0.0468 0.0108 0.0312
2017 0.0949 0.0272 -0.0765 -0.0361 -0.0916
2018 0.0251 0.0416 0.0498 -0.1487 0.0911
2019 0.0520 0.0647 0.0654 0.0669 -0.1096
``` ::: ::: ::: {#cell-fig-placebo .cell execution_count=11} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ![Placebo matrix in GJ per m2: each design-year contrast applied to every field year. The diagonal is the matched pairing.](uniform_deployment_files/figure-html/fig-placebo-output-1.png){#fig-placebo width=575 height=451} ::: ::: ::: {#tbl-placebo-summary .cell execution_count=12} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=36} ```{=html}
quantity value
0 matched mean -0.0709
1 mismatched mean 0.0184
2 mismatched sd 0.0618
3 matched - mismatched -0.0893
4 field-label permutation p 0.0331
``` ::: ::: All five matched values are negative, against a mismatched mean of $+0.018$. The matched-minus- mismatched contrast is $-0.089$ GJ m$^{-2}$, and permuting **field** labels — a null that absorbs any amount of design drift, since drift makes $\Delta_k$ nonzero whatever field it meets. Two nulls resting on different assumptions therefore agree. The second is the weaker claim (only 120 labellings exist, so its floor is $1/121$) but it does not need D1a. The finding is not an artefact of the residual drift. The contrast with the real-deployment arm is sharp. There, matched (0.128) was *smaller* than mismatched (0.239), ratio 0.54, field-label $p = 0.70$ — consistent with a drifting contrast projecting onto whatever field it meets, and no detectable preferential sampling. Here matched exceeds mismatched and both nulls reject. Cleaning up the deployment design did not weaken the test; it revealed a signal the contaminated arm could not. ## What this means for the test as specified 1. **The uniform arm should carry the primary test.** Its D1a violation is $3.3\times$ smaller, and the placebo confirms the conclusion survives dropping D1a entirely. The real-deployment arm is interpretable only with the placebo calibration attached. 2. **D1a should be stated as approximate, with the violation reported.** No deployment design makes it exact, because uniformly seeded floats still advect into year-varying concentration. The honest form is an assumption plus a measured bound, not an assumption asserted. 3. **Report the placebo alongside $\hat p_{\mathrm{pool}}$, not as a footnote.** It is the only quantity that separates drift from alignment, and it is what turns a D1a-dependent rejection into a defensible one. 4. **Replication is the binding constraint, not velocity years.** At 10 replicates the Monte-Carlo floor was 0.089 GJ m$^{-2}$, comparable to $\bar T$ itself; at 190 it is small enough for a 3-sigma result. Extending $D$ is cheaper than extending $M$ and buys more here. ## Caveats - **A proxy, not the OSSE.** Pure horizontal advection at the park depth: no ascent, no surface drift, no profile-time trapping. The occupancy structure is right; the magnitude of $\bar T$ from the full park-and-profile simulation may differ. - **One box, one depth.** Box B (35–45 N, 60–40 W) at 0–2000 m. Box A, the quiescent Sargasso control, would say whether the effect tracks eddy activity. - **$B_{\mathrm{dep}}$ is not yet computable.** The argo arm still seeds every float on 1 Jan while the uniform arm is staggered, so their difference confounds deployment geography with release timing. A matched re-run of the argo arm with its empirical day-of-year is needed before the decomposition at the top of this report can be evaluated. - **The residual field carries the mean-field specification.** $\tilde Z$ is a residual from a quadratic-plus-harmonics fit from 1995; a spatially *uniform* misfit cancels identically in $B$, but a spatially varying one does not.
